headline: Net revenue -EUR 731,270 (-7.18%) YoY.
finding: Net revenue fell EUR 731,270 (-7.18%) in H2 2025 against H2 2024 (EUR 10,188,728 to EUR 9,457,457), week-aligned retail weeks 27 to 52.
supporting_analysis: headline_trend.csv; reconciled to Phase 4 within EUR 0.01 (phase5_validation_report.md)
business_interpretation: The decline is real and measured on the governed definition; it is the quantity every other finding explains a part of.
recommended_next_analysis: None: this is the target of the Phase 6 root-cause case.
limitations: Synthetic data; excludes VAT; returns counted on the return date at the returning store.
impact_basis: Total change in net revenue

headline: Decline begins with H2 (H1 +1.4%); 20 of 26 H2 weeks down.
finding: The decline starts at the beginning of H2: H1 2025 was +1.4% YoY, the rolling 4-week YoY turns negative in week 30 and stays negative to week 52. 20 of 26 weeks are down. Weeks 27 to 31 average -1.4%, weeks 32 to 52 average -8.8%.
business_interpretation: Pattern: a persistent decline with no clear trend within the period (persistent; step test R2 0.12, linear trend R2 0.01, weeks 27-39 -7.1% vs weeks 40-52 -7.3%). The five weakest weeks (W50, W52, W35, W38, W44) carry 55% of the decline.
recommended_next_analysis: Date the onset per store and category in Phase 6 and match it to operational events.
limitations: Weekly YoY is noisy (single weeks move by +/-20%); the step test is descriptive, not a formal change-point test. On the full-year series (whose rolling window includes late-H1 weeks) the rolling YoY stays negative from week 29.
impact_basis: Not a EUR driver (timing only)

headline: Fewer transactions: -EUR 614,363 (84% of the fall).
finding: Fewer transactions account for -EUR 614,363 of the change (84% of it): receipts fell 5.85% (229,446 to 216,027).
business_interpretation: Most of the decline is fewer customer visits (receipts), not smaller or cheaper baskets.
recommended_next_analysis: Split the transaction fall by store and week (see the store findings) and test traffic explanations in Phase 6.
limitations: Transactions are receipts, a proxy for visits; no footfall data exists to separate traffic from conversion.
impact_basis: Shapley transactions effect within Sales Revenue

headline: Basket size and price: -EUR 102,250 combined (14% of the fall).
finding: Basket effects: UPT -EUR 34,173 (UPT 2.127 to 2.120) and ASP -EUR 68,077 (ASP EUR 21.63 to EUR 21.49); AOV changed -1.00%.
business_interpretation: At estate level spend per visit moved -1.0%; the estate ASP hides larger category movements (largest category ASP effect: Home & Kitchen -EUR 178,055).
recommended_next_analysis: Decompose ASP into like-for-like price, discount and mix effects by category in Phase 6.
limitations: Estate ASP mixes price, discount depth and category mix; segment bridges do not add up to the estate bridge.
impact_basis: Shapley UPT + ASP effects within Sales Revenue

headline: Higher returns: -EUR 14,657.
finding: Higher returns reduce net revenue by a further EUR 14,657: returns value EUR 368,713 to EUR 383,371; return rate by value 3.49% to 3.90%.
business_interpretation: Returns are 2% of the estate decline; they rose while sales fell, so the return rate rose faster than the returns value.
recommended_next_analysis: See the returns concentration finding.
limitations: Returns are dated at the return, not the original sale.
impact_basis: Minus the change in Returns Value

headline: 3 stores (S03, S04, S05) carry 62% of the fall (-EUR 449,972).
finding: 3 stores (S03 Dublin Blanchardstown, S04 Dublin Swords, S05 Dublin Tallaght; region Dublin and format Standard) account for 62% of the decline (-EUR 449,972; -29.2% YoY). The other 17 stores together are -3.3%.
business_interpretation: The decline is concentrated, not estate-wide. Transactions YoY in these stores: -30%, -27%, -27%; their transactions effect is -EUR 440,100 of their -EUR 449,972.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: store-week and daypart timing of the transaction fall in these stores; compare with the other stores in the same region.
limitations: Store results rely on complete store-day coverage (1 store-week gap(s) found, see Data coverage).
impact_basis: Sum of the stores' net revenue change

headline: Their fall is abrupt (from week 28) and persistent, about -31% a week.
finding: In the 3 stores the fall is abrupt and persistent: their weekly YoY is negative in every week from week 28 and averages -31% after it, while the other stores average -3.5% per week (range -19% to +13%).
metric: Weekly Net Revenue YoY % (cluster vs rest)
business_interpretation: Transactions explain 98% of these stores' fall and it starts within weeks of the start of H2 in all of them: the signature of a local event rather than an estate-wide trading problem.
recommended_next_analysis: Identify what changed at these stores around that week (Phase 6).
limitations: Timing is inferred from weekly data; exact dates need store operational logs.
impact_basis: Not a EUR driver (timing only)

headline: Hypothesis: a local traffic event around S03, S04, S05 may have reduced visits.
finding: Hypothesis: a local, traffic-related change may have hit the region Dublin / format Standard stores (for example a new competitor, access or roadworks disruption, or a local footfall shift), reducing visits from early H2.
business_interpretation: Consistent with the pattern (visits down, basket stable, timing shared), but nothing in the model records competitors, footfall or local events.
recommended_next_analysis: Obtain footfall counts, competitor openings, local events and store operating logs for these stores; compare same-region stores that did not decline.
limitations: Additional data required: the available data cannot confirm or reject this.
impact_basis: Cluster change (same slice as above)

headline: Dublin: 69% of the fall, mostly its Standard-format stores.
finding: Dublin contributes -EUR 503,056 (69% of the decline, -13.7%); 5 of 5 of its stores declined, but the split by format is uneven: Standard -29.2% (-EUR 449,972); Flagship -2.5% (-EUR 53,084).
business_interpretation: The regional figure is driven by specific stores; a region-wide explanation would have to explain why other formats in the region held up.
recommended_next_analysis: Treat the store cluster, not the region, as the unit of investigation.
limitations: Region and format are confounded in a 20-store estate (few stores per cell).
impact_basis: Region's net revenue change

headline: Electronics & Tech: -EUR 268,518 (37% of the fall), mainly transactions.
finding: Electronics & Tech contributes -EUR 268,518 (37% of the decline, -11.8%). Largest components: transactions (receipts containing the category) -EUR 242,992, returns -EUR 26,289. Availability 95.4% to 89.3%, promo share 9.7% to 12.9%, return rate 5.7% to 7.6%, gross margin 18.7% to 15.6%. 53% of the category's decline is in Dublin. Estimated lost sales from stock-outs rose EUR 37,235 (ESTIMATE).
business_interpretation: Fewer receipts contain the category; with estate traffic down this is partly the store cluster and partly category-specific (availability or range).
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: separate the part of this category's fall that belongs to the store cluster from the part spread across the estate.
limitations: Category transactions are receipts containing the category (not additive across categories).
impact_basis: Category's net revenue change

headline: Home & Kitchen: -EUR 239,994 (33% of the fall), mainly ASP.
finding: Home & Kitchen contributes -EUR 239,994 (33% of the decline, -9.3%). Largest components: ASP -EUR 178,055, transactions (receipts containing the category) -EUR 101,977. Availability 95.1% to 95.9%, promo share 12.7% to 27.6%, return rate 4.0% to 3.9%, gross margin 42.8% to 36.8%. 59% of the category's decline is in Dublin.
business_interpretation: The category sells at a lower price per unit; discounting and mix are the candidate mechanisms.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: separate the part of this category's fall that belongs to the store cluster from the part spread across the estate.
limitations: Category transactions are receipts containing the category (not additive across categories).
impact_basis: Category's net revenue change

headline: Availability fell 6.1 pp in Electronics & Tech (estate -0.65 pp).
finding: Estate availability moved from 95.4% to 94.8% (-0.65 pp), but Electronics & Tech fell 6.1 pp (95.4% to 89.3%); by supply source the largest drops in that category are Unknown supplier -21.8 pp; Voltix Distribution Ltd -12.5 pp.
supporting_analysis: availability_diagnostics.csv (levels Estate, Category, Supplier x Category, Week)
business_interpretation: The availability problem is narrow: 1 category fell by 2 pp or more, and within it particular supply sources.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: replenishment history (received quantities, order and delivery data) for the affected supplier's SKUs.
limitations: Availability counts store-SKU-weeks with zero closing stock; it does not see part-week stock-outs that recovered.
impact_basis: Not a EUR figure (see the estimated lost sales finding)

headline: Full-week stock-outs cost an estimated EUR 37,261 more (ESTIMATE), mostly Electronics & Tech.
finding: ESTIMATE: in store-SKU-weeks with no stock at any point (opening stock 0, nothing received) sales were 0 units against 434 expected; the estimated sales lost in such weeks rose from EUR 19 to EUR 37,280 (EUR 37,261, 5% of the decline). Electronics & Tech accounts for EUR 37,235, Voltix Distribution Ltd SKUs for EUR 30,996.
metric: Estimated Lost Sales (BR-05, ESTIMATE, full-week stock-outs)
supporting_analysis: availability_diagnostics.csv, lost_sales_method_check.csv; back-test of the expected level on in-stock, non-promoted weeks: actual/expected 0.993 (WAPE 12.5% at store x category x week). Rule: weeks with no stock all week sold at most 60% of expected: met; estimator back-test bias within +/-15%: met; at least 90% of stock-out weeks have a baseline: met.
business_interpretation: Stock-outs are a visible, quantified mechanism behind part of the decline: where there was no stock there were no sales, and the expected sales are estimated with a back-tested baseline.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: confirm with replenishment data why these SKUs went out of stock.
limitations: An estimate (conservative): assumes demand equals the store-SKU's nearby in-stock, non-promoted rate adjusted by the category's weekly seasonality; ignores substitution to other SKUs; excludes partial-week stock-outs (next finding).
impact_basis: Increase in estimated lost sales, full-week stock-outs (negative = revenue lost)

headline: Hypothesis: partial-week stock-outs may have cost up to EUR 60,389 more.
finding: Hypothesis: partial-week stock-outs (restocked or sold out during the week) may have cost up to EUR 60,389 more. Literal BR-05 upper bound over all stock-out weeks: EUR 4,461 to EUR 102,112.
metric: Estimated Lost Sales (BR-05 upper bound, ESTIMATE)
business_interpretation: Not evidence: in aggregate these weeks sold more than expected, and the per-week clipped estimate reports EUR 13.4 per in-stock week where nothing was lost (noise floor) against EUR 3.1 per partial stock-out week.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: daily or intraday stock positions (or till timestamps) to date when each SKU ran out.
limitations: Additional data required: the weekly snapshot cannot show how long a SKU was out within the week.
impact_basis: Upper bound minus the full-week estimate (not additional evidence)

headline: Store availability change does not track store revenue change (r = -0.24, p = 0.31).
finding: Across stores, availability change and revenue change are not significantly related (Pearson r = -0.24, p = 0.31, n = 20). Across store x category cells, larger increases in estimated lost sales go with larger revenue falls (r = -0.33, p = 0.0001, n = 140; Spearman rho = -0.30).
business_interpretation: Availability does not explain which stores declined most (store cluster availability change -0.55 pp on average, estate -0.65 pp). The cell-level link is consistent across cells.
recommended_next_analysis: No further correlation work; use the SKU-level lost-sales estimate instead.
limitations: Correlation, not causation; small n for stores; cell-level result driven by outliers.
impact_basis: Not a EUR figure

headline: Hypothesis: a supply problem with Voltix Distribution Ltd may have caused the Electronics & Tech stock-outs.
finding: Hypothesis: a replenishment or supply problem with Voltix Distribution Ltd (Electronics & Tech) may have caused the stock-outs (availability 95.2% to 82.7%, EUR 30,996 of the full-week lost-sales estimate increase).
business_interpretation: The availability drop follows the supplier: Voltix Distribution Ltd Electronics & Tech availability 95.2% to 82.7% across the estate; store execution alone would not follow one supplier.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: received_qty and closing-stock sequences for the supplier's SKUs; request purchase orders, delivery confirmations and supplier fill-rate data.
limitations: Additional data required: the model has stock and receipts but no orders or supplier communications. Some affected SKUs have no supplier on the product master ('Unknown supplier'), which limits the supplier view.
impact_basis: The supplier's slice of the full-week lost-sales estimate (same slice as the lost-sales finding)

headline: 'Faulty' returns in Electronics & Tech up EUR 31,589; 4 store x category cells hold 56% of the increase.
finding: Returns rose where one recorded reason rose: 'Faulty' returns in Electronics & Tech went from EUR 35,190 to EUR 66,778 (EUR 31,589), while the estate total rose EUR 14,657. 4 store x category cells hold 56% of the gross increase: S07 Electronics & Tech, S13 Electronics & Tech, S14 Electronics & Tech, S15 Electronics & Tech.
supporting_analysis: returns_diagnostics.csv (levels Category x Reason, Store x Category, Product), figures/07_returns_trend.png
business_interpretation: The returns increase is concentrated in a few store and category cells, not a general change in customer behaviour.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: 'Faulty' returns by product, supplier and original sale date (batch timing).
limitations: return_reason is the reason recorded at the till, not a verified fault.
impact_basis: Increase in returns in that category and reason

headline: Hypothesis: a quality problem in some Electronics & Tech products may have raised 'Faulty' returns.
finding: Hypothesis: a product quality problem in specific Electronics & Tech products may have increased 'Faulty' returns.
business_interpretation: Plausible given the reason code, but the data cannot distinguish a genuine defect from a change in how staff record reasons.
recommended_next_analysis: Request supplier batch or lot data, QA inspections and customer complaint logs.
limitations: Additional data required.
impact_basis: Same slice as the returns finding above

headline: Discount cost up EUR 259,341; promo share 12.7% to 16.9%.
finding: Promotion intensity rose: promo revenue share 12.7% to 16.9%, discount cost EUR 269,584 to EUR 528,924, average discount depth 16.7% to 24.1%, promoted-line margin 31.5% to 24.3%.
metric: Promo Revenue Share %, Promo Discount Cost
business_interpretation: More revenue now comes through discounted sales; discount cost is 2.0x the prior year.
recommended_next_analysis: See the category promotion finding.
limitations: Discount cost reduces Sales Revenue directly, but without promotions some of the volume would not exist; it is not a net loss.
impact_basis: Not a net revenue effect (discount cost; its revenue effect sits in the ASP effects)

headline: Home & Kitchen promotions: 3.6x the events, deeper discounts, incremental margin -EUR 33,508; ASP effect -EUR 178,055.
finding: Home & Kitchen: promotion events 2,427 to 8,848, average discount 15% to 32%, uplift 90% to 176% but incremental promo margin EUR 26,974 to -EUR 33,508; post-promotion weeks -16% vs baseline. Category ASP -6.7%, gross margin 42.8% to 36.8%.
business_interpretation: Deeper, more frequent promotions in Home & Kitchen lifted promoted volume but did not pay for their discount; the category's revenue fell mainly through a lower selling price.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: category-week counterfactual (sales with and without promotion), cannibalisation of non-promoted SKUs.
limitations: Uplift uses a pre-promotion baseline of the same store-SKU (seasonally adjusted); overlapping promotions are excluded.
impact_basis: Category ASP effect (Shapley)

headline: Post-promotion dip -12% and -13% vs baseline (prior, current year).
finding: Pull-forward: estate post-promotion weeks are -12.1% (H2 2024) and -12.9% (H2 2025) against baseline.
business_interpretation: Some demand is pulled forward in both years; the estate-level dip barely changed, so pull-forward alone does not explain the decline.
recommended_next_analysis: Include post-promotion dips in the Phase 6 promotion counterfactual.
limitations: Two post weeks only; measured against an estimated baseline.
impact_basis: Not a EUR figure

headline: Hypothesis: the Home & Kitchen promotion programme may have reduced revenue.
finding: Hypothesis: the Home & Kitchen promotion programme may have reduced revenue (price investment without enough incremental volume, and cannibalisation of full-price sales).
business_interpretation: Consistent with the measured changes, but a counterfactual (what would have sold without the promotions) is needed.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: counterfactual by category-week; promotion calendar and planning rationale from Marketing.
limitations: Additional analysis required; association between promotion intensity and revenue is not causation.
impact_basis: Same slice as the category promotion finding

headline: 16 of 20 stores persistently miss target (16 in the prior year); an outcome, not a cause.
finding: 16 of 20 stores meet the BRD persistent-underperformance rule (missed 8+ of the last 13 weeks) in H2 2025, against 16 in H2 2024; estate target achievement 92.8% to 86.6%. Lowest in H2 2025: S03 63%, S04 67%, S05 72%.
business_interpretation: Target misses are an outcome, not a cause. Because most stores missed in both years, the rule does not separate the declining stores from the rest; achievement % ranks them better.
recommended_next_analysis: Review how targets are set with Finance before using misses as a performance signal.
limitations: Targets are Finance plans; store-weeks without a target: 3 (H2 2024), 0 (H2 2025). Variance to target H2 2025: -EUR 1,458,583.
impact_basis: Not a net revenue effect (outcome vs plan)

headline: Range churn: -EUR 144,052 delisted, EUR 415,173 new SKUs (net EUR 271,121).
finding: Range churn: SKUs sold only in H2 2024 had EUR 144,052 (16 SKUs); SKUs sold only in H2 2025 took EUR 415,173 (22 SKUs); net EUR 271,121. Largest net churn: Electronics & Tech EUR 168,187, where SKUs sold in both periods changed -EUR 436,705.
metric: Net revenue of delisted and new SKUs
business_interpretation: Measured only: new SKUs brought revenue while continuing SKUs fell in the same category; whether the new SKUs added sales or replaced (cannibalised) existing ones is not tested.
recommended_next_analysis: Phase 6: test cannibalisation between new and continuing SKUs by category and store.
limitations: Delisting is inferred from sales and ranging, not from a range-plan record.
impact_basis: Net revenue of SKUs sold in one period only

headline: S13: 2 missing prior-year trading days (about EUR 11,175), flatters its YoY.
finding: S13 has 2 fewer trading days than other stores in retail week 42 of 2024 (no sales recorded); at its average daily net revenue this is about EUR 11,175 of prior-year revenue missing, which flatters its YoY.
business_interpretation: Too small to change any conclusion; disclosed so the store's YoY is read correctly.
recommended_next_analysis: None needed for Phase 6; flag in store-level reporting.
limitations: The cause of the gap (closure or missing data) is not recorded in the model.
impact_basis: Not a net revenue effect (data coverage)
